Subject: Internal: initial findings for Clarity Bank latency spike (INC-7248)

Grace / Ben — quick technical notes from the runtime team after initial triage: 

1) Timeline (UTC):
- 02:37:14: sudden surge of small synchronous calls originating from three Clarity service nodes (normal pattern amplified by an upstream retry loop)
- 02:39:50: autoscaler triggered scale-up; control-plane commands delayed ~20s due to lock contention during simultaneous scale ops
- 02:40:30–03:05: queue growth + increased KV cache misses leading to longer token-serve latency; p95 rose to ~2.5s; tail spiked ~4s
- 03:06:02: autoscaler recovered; backlog cleared by 03:14 UTC

2) Root cause (preliminary): interaction between autoscaler leader election and a latent rate-smoothing bug in the batch-assigner that allowed a retry storm to amplify normal client retries. When combined, the control-plane experienced lock contention and delayed worker attachment.

3) Scope and data sensitivity: at this time we see no indication of request data leakage or unauthorized access. All affected requests were authenticated and served within existing isolation boundaries.

4) Immediate mitigations applied (02:55–03:20 UTC):
- Hotfix: disabled aggressive retry smoothing for the assigner
- Increased autoscaler lock timeouts and added a short jitter on leader election to avoid simultaneous control-plane ops
- Temporarily raised per-account concurrency caps for Clarity to drain backlog faster

I’ve uploaded a draft RCA and the CSV timeline to the incident folder (links below). Next steps: produce a customer-facing RCA, add a permanent fix to the assigner, and add regression tests.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/claritybank-incident-20280315
Attachments: clarity_rca_draft.pdf, clarity_incident_timeline.csv

— Marcus

Subject: Clarity Bank — incident report and remediation commitments (Mar 15, 2028)

Hi Marta / Rajiv —

Thank you again for raising this promptly. Below is a concise customer-facing summary of what happened, what we changed, and how we will verify the fix. Please let me know if you need any additional artifacts for your compliance review.

Executive summary:
- What happened: between 02:37–03:14 UTC on 2028-03-15, your inference requests experienced elevated latency and short timeouts due to a combined retry amplification and autoscaler coordination issue.
- Impact: increased p95 latency (baseline ~120ms → ~2.5s); a small fraction of scheduled batch jobs retried and timed out.
- Data: no evidence of data leakage or unauthorized access.

Root cause (short): a latent bug in the batch-assigner allowed client-side retries to amplify, and concurrent autoscaler leader events created control-plane lock contention that delayed worker attachment. Full technical detail in attached RCA.

Immediate mitigations applied (already live):
- Disabled aggressive retry smoothing in the assigner (hotfix).
- Increased autoscaler lock tolerance and added election jitter.
- Temporarily increased per-account concurrency for Clarity to speed backlog drain.

Planned permanent actions and timeline:
- Week 1 (Mar 16–22): ship a tested fix for the assigner logic; add unit + integration tests to prevent regression.
- Week 2 (Mar 23–29): roll out staged canary to 10% of accounts, monitor for amplification; add automated alert if observed.
- Week 3 (Apr 1–5): full rollout to all regions and post-rollout verification sweep against your scheduled jobs.

Verification and evidence for compliance:
- We will provide the following artifacts by Apr 12, 2028: incident timeline (CSV), signed RCA (PDF), and a remediation verification report (MD) showing test results and production metrics.
- If you require SOC/attestation snippets, we can include relevant audit log extracts under your NDA.

Attachments: clarity_rca_draft.pdf, clarity_incident_timeline.csv, remediation-verification-plan.md
Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/claritybank-incident-20280315, https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-7248

Next steps: Ben will schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week to go over the RCA and answer questions. Grace will follow up with the verification artifacts by Apr 12.

Apologies for the disruption — we take reliability seriously and will prioritize preventing recurrence.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Redwood Inference
